title: Prefetch surgeon notes (midnight)
content:
Date: 2025-10-22
Shift: midnight (solo) — quick capture before handing off to Nilima in the morning
Context: customer-prod observed intermittent p99 token latency spikes correlated with long prompt sequences. Root suspicion: prefetch/eviction interplay with small LRU slices on multi-GPU nodes (NVLink topology variance).

Observations from the incident (logs at /var/log/serving/runtime/2025-10-22/spike-0821.log):
- Spike windows: ~08:21, 09:04 UTC — spikes last ~15–30s, p99 jumps from 120ms -> 820ms for generation steps around token 5k–9k.
- Worker-level metrics show KV cache hit-rate drops from 98% -> 42% in the same window.
- Kernel traces: repeated evict->fetch patterns on the same attention layer (attn_kv_layer_10) across workers co-located on same NUMA domain.
- dmesg shows occasional nvlink timeouts on GPU1 (stack trace t=09:03), but not persistent.

Quick repro attempt (local):
1) Use small reproducer model (gpt-small-ish) with scripted long-context generator: 12k tokens input + streaming generation to force deep KV occupancy.
2) Run two workers pinned to same NUMA node, batch size=1, unbatched concurrency 8.
3) Toggle prefetch policy: off / conservative / aggressive.
Outcome: aggressive prefetch causes earlier cache pressure (expected), conservative results in more fetches but slightly lower instant eviction churn. Repro is noisy but directionally similar to prod.

Hypotheses (ranked):
A) Eviction storms triggered by prefetch aggressive heuristics + small per-worker cache slices -> concurrent evict/fetch thrash -> temporary loss of locality -> p99 spikes.
B) NVLink hiccups amplify latency when remote KV fetchs fall back to PCIe (timeout path) for a few seconds. dmesg evidence weak but present.
C) Batch packing changes (recent scheduler tweak PR#2782) increased variance in typical seq-lengths per worker -> cache fragmentation across workers.

Immediate mitigations to try (fast, revertable):
- Toggle prefetch from "aggressive" -> "balanced" for the customer ring (canary) (low blast radius). (Owner: Arjun, quick command: POST /api/v1/configs/prefetch?policy=balanced --env=canary)
- Enforce per-worker soft guarding: worker_cache_soft_limit = 0.82 * worker_cache_alloc to delay evictions (temp param).
- Add a micro-rate limiter to prefetch tasks when pending_evictions > threshold to avoid bursty simultaneous fetches.

Commands I ran / snippets (save for runbook):
- tail -n 200 /var/log/serving/runtime/2025-10-22/spike-0821.log | grep -i evict
- sudo perf record -a -g -o /tmp/perf.data -- sleep 30 (on canary node, 09:10)
- python tools/repro_long_context.py --model gpt-small --seq 12000 --workers 2 --prefetch aggressive

Metrics to capture (add to canary dashboard):
- kv.cache.hit_rate per-worker (1s resolution)
- kv.cache.eviction_rate per-worker
- prefetch.pending_tasks
- kernel.nvlink_errors (nvlink hardware counters)
- scheduler.batch_length_variance
- os.numa_remote_access_rate

Longer-run experiments (need cycle / coordination):
- Experiment E1: Increase per-worker cache slice by 25% and measure p99 across days (risk: higher memory footprint across nodes). (Coord: Infra/Platform)
- Experiment E2: Introduce jitter in prefetch start times (stagger prefetch across workers floor(random(0,50ms))). This reduces synchronized eviction waves. (Low-risk; code change in prefetch scheduler)
- Experiment E3: Fallback path hardening: when nvlink errors spike, prefer local-cache-prefetch-to-disk rather than remote fetch to avoid timeout penalty. (Requires infra/driver discussion)

Notes to self / heuristics discovered tonight:
- When two high-KV workers land on the same NUMA socket, eviction storms are far more likely. Pinning strategy might need 'anti-colocate-high-kv' heuristic.
- The token-position where p99 climbs is often the point where attention layers' kv size crosses a 4MB boundary — looks like a threshold in our allocator behavior (investigate allocator cut-offs).
- PR#2782 changed the "pack-seq" fast-path to be more permissive; need to double-check side-effect on per-worker effective cache slice size.

Handoff checklist for Nilima (AM):
- Summary: observed p99 spikes due to KV cache thrash; temporary mitigation: switch prefetch->balanced on canary, enable soft_limit param.
- Morning tasks (priority):
  1) Validate canary metrics after policy flip (dashboard: INF-kv-canary). Check p99 over 1h window vs prior 6h.
  2) Pull perf.data from canary node and run Flamegraph (tools/fg.py /tmp/perf.data). Look for repeated 'evict_kv' frames.
  3) Check node GPU1 nvlink logs (sudo dmesg | grep nvlink) for 10/22 08:15-09:15 UTC. Attach to Jira INF-4829.
  4) If canary shows improvement, coordinate with Liam to roll to prod little-by-little (1% -> 5% -> 20%).

Unresolved questions (write up before next week design doc):
- Is allocator boundary around 4MB a software artifact (jemalloc/our allocator) or driver-side? (Action: grep allocator release notes / check jemalloc arenas config).
- Do we have metrics for per-layer KV distribution (by byte-size) across workers? If not, add logging hook in runtime.
- Would staggered prefetch create cold-miss cascades that amplify tail for very deep sequences? Need simulation.

Random quick TODOs (for personal memory):
- File small perf flamegraph in INF-4829 and tag Liam + Nilima.
- Add unit test for prefetch backpressure threshold (simulate N concurrent evict tasks -> expect tasks to queue).
- Draft mini-runbook entry: "If p99 spike with KV-hit drop, flip prefetch->balanced, set worker_cache_soft_limit, escalate if nvlink errors > 5/min".

Closing notes (notes-to-self style):
- Keep change small tonight; prefer config flip over code change.
- Capture as much ephemeral telemetry as possible before rolling anything back.
- If we see NVLink errors persist, loop in HW infra and open support ticket with cloud provider (include dmesg).

End of capture. Passing to Nilima for morning follow-up.

Signature: Arjun (quick, messy — will tidy if we turn into a runbook)
